ruleName: Relief for Ball in Penalty Area
imagePrompt: Create a modern semi-realistic illustration (about 75% realistic, 25% stylised) in the established junior golf quiz style. Show a female golfer preparing to play a shot with her ball lying inside a clearly marked red penalty area. A red penalty area stake, embedded firmly in the ground, is positioned so it would interfere with her swing. The stake must be obviously unmovable. The scene should convey that the golfer cannot take relief due to rules. Do not include any text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards or speech bubbles.
imageAlt: A female golfer preparing to swing at a ball located inside a red penalty area, with an immovable red stake interfering with her swing path.

sceneSpec.setting: Edge of a golf course penalty area, red stakes visible
sceneSpec.players: One female golfer preparing for a shot
sceneSpec.ballPosition: Ball lying clearly within a red penalty area, close to an immovable red stake embedded in the ground
sceneSpec.ruleMoment: The golfer is addressing the ball and the stake is affecting her swing path
sceneSpec.educationalFocus: Clarifies that no free relief is provided from a penalty area stake interfering with a stroke from within the penalty area
mustShow: Red penalty area stake secured in the ground
Golf ball inside the penalty area, near the stake
Golfer preparing to swing with the stake interfering
mustNotShow: Numbers, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, captions, club crests, scorecards or speech bubbles

questions.title: Can Emma get a free drop if a red stake is in her way in the penalty area?
questions.question: Emma's ball is in the red area by a pond. There is a red post stuck in the ground, and she can't move it. The post is in the way of her swing. Can Emma take a free drop away from the post?

choices.text: Yes, because the post cannot be moved.
Yes, because the post is in the way of her swing.

questions.explanation: Emma cannot get a free drop from the red post if her ball is in the penalty area. She has to play the ball as it is or take a penalty drop.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A place with red or yellow lines or posts, like a pond or stream, where special rules apply.
A drop where you don’t get a penalty.
Something you cannot move, like a post stuck in concrete.

questions.teachingTip: Help children look for colour markers on the course and explain that the rules are different in those areas.
likelyMisconceptions: Kids may think they can always move their ball away from things in the penalty area.
They might believe all posts or signs give free drops.

questions.title: Is free relief given for a penalty-area stake interfering with a swing?
questions.question: Emma’s ball lies in a red penalty area. One of the red stakes interferes with her swing. The stake is embedded in concrete and cannot be moved. Is Emma entitled to free relief from the stake?

choices.text: Yes, because the stake is an immovable obstruction.
Yes, but only because it interferes with her swing.

questions.explanation: No free relief is available from immovable obstructions such as penalty area stakes when the ball lies in a penalty area. The Rules do not allow relief for an artificial object in these circumstances.
